FINDING_ID: F001  
SEVERITY: 0.95  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.85  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` claims to use live-updated fingerprints for adaptive routing, but `LoadBalancer` never consults model fingerprints or role capability scores when allocating tasks. Its greedy heuristic uses only admissibility, current load fraction, token limits, and criticality. As implemented, fingerprint updates have no effect on allocation decisions, so the advertised adaptive routing feedback loop is functionally absent. This matters because a major architectural claim of the module is untrue, and downstream orchestration may rely on adaptive specialization that never occurs.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Incorporate capability/fingerprint-based suitability into allocation. For example, define per-task/model utility from role weights, flaw-class specialization, historical performance, or fingerprint-derived score, and include it in the greedy ranking or objective. Update `LoadBalancer._solve_greedy()` and/or `_objective()` to prefer models with stronger live fingerprints for the relevant task.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.90  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler` exclusion is not reflected in the active set for PM abort logic. In `get_recovery()`, PM repeated transport/protocol failures return `ABORT`, but the PM is not removed from `_active_models`. `should_abort()` then only aborts because of the explicit PM-not-active check if PM was excluded, which never happens on ABORT. More broadly, the active set and recovery semantics are inconsistent: `EXCLUDE` mutates active state, `ABORT` does not. This matters because state-based consumers may observe a still-active PM after a terminal abort-worthy failure, leading to contradictory orchestration state.  
PROPOSED_FIX: On `ABORT`, either remove the model from `_active_models` or treat abort as an independent terminal state and document that active set is no longer meaningful after abort. Ensure `process_round()` propagates a consistent post-abort active model state.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80  
DESCRIPTION: The PM failure escalation threshold is off by one relative to the configuration name and comments. `repeated = same_type_count >= self.config.n_fail` is computed before recording the current failure. With default `n_fail=2`, ABORT/EXCLUDE occurs on the third occurrence, not the second. The inline validator comment in `FailureHandler.validate_k1()` acknowledges this mismatch. This matters because operational recovery policy is materially different from the stated threshold.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either redefine the condition as `(same_type_count + 1) >= n_fail` if `n_fail` means total occurrences including current, or rename/document `n_fail` as “prior failures before escalation.” Update comments and validators accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits the wrong event type for format violations. When `format_compliant` is false, it emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` instead of `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`, despite returning `FailureType.FORMAT`. This matters because monitoring consumers cannot distinguish parse failures from format violations, defeating the typed event interface and corrupting telemetry/recovery analytics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the emitted event type in the format-violation branch to `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. Add a test asserting event/failure-type consistency.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` only runs failure detection for models present in the `responses` dict. Missing responses are not treated as failures, even though absence of a response is operationally equivalent to timeout/empty transport failure in this management layer. This matters because a model can silently disappear from a round without being penalized, excluded, or counted toward critical failure, making failure handling incomplete and unsafe.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compare expected active models for the round against received `responses`. For missing models, synthesize a timeout/missing-response failure record and process recovery.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006  
SEVERITY: 0.85  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` can reinstall the locked PM into `role_map` even if the PM is not in `active_models`. It always starts `new_map = {self.pm_model_id: Role.PM}` without checking activeness. This creates an inconsistent map where inactive or excluded PM remains assigned, and downstream components that use `role_map` may treat the PM as active.  
PROPOSED_FIX: If PM is not in `active_models`, either abort immediately, or return a map containing only active models and let terminal failure handling own the PM-loss case. Do not force inactive models into the new role map.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` uses `if len(self._models) >= 3:` to decide whether to assign a COL role, instead of using the number of active models. If the original pool had 3+ models but only 2 remain active, it still assigns one of them as COL, contrary to the initial assignment logic comment “Assign COL (if K >= 3)” and contrary to reduction behavior by active topology. This matters because dynamic reassignment no longer respects reduced active-pool semantics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace `len(self._models) >= 3` with `len(active_models) >= 3` when deciding whether COL exists in the current round.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.kappa_adopt()` does not validate or clamp `adoption_delta`. If callers pass values outside [0,1], `kappa_adopt` leaves the intended [0,1] range despite the docstring claiming it returns a value in [0,1]. This can make `kappa()` negative or greater than 1 via `min(ks, kr, ka)`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `adoption_delta` on input in `add_round_findings()` or clamp in `kappa_adopt()` with `min(max(1.0 - delta, 0.0), 1.0)`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.kappa_set()` can return negative values, contradicting its docstring. If severity of novel classes exceeds cumulative aggregated severity due to duplicate aggregation effects or invalid severity inputs, `1 - novel/total` becomes negative. The docstring states the return is in [0,1], but there is no clamp and no validation of finding severities.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `Finding.severity` in [0,1] and clamp `kappa_set` into [0,1].  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F010  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: Several core numeric fields are undocumentedly unvalidated: `CapabilityFingerprint` fields, `Task.criticality`, `Finding.severity`, `Finding.abstraction_index`, `ModelSpec.L_std`, costs, token limits, and many config thresholds besides `tau_kappa` and `feasibility_threshold`. The module repeatedly assumes these are in constrained ranges. Invalid inputs can produce impossible probabilities, negative costs, nonsensical scoring, or invalid convergence metrics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `__post_init__` validation for all dataclasses and full config range checks for thresholds/weights.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F011  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: The correlated failure model is architecturally disconnected from failure handling and orchestration. `DynamicManager` instantiates `CorrelatedFailureModel`, but neither allocation, dispatch feasibility, failure recovery, nor abort policy uses it. The artifact claims this as a management-layer extension, but it is effectively dead functionality outside the smoke test.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Integrate correlated failure risk into allocation/redundancy policy, dispatch decisions, or abort thresholds. For example, penalize assigning all critical tasks to highly correlated model sets.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F012  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: The “real-time manager monitoring interface” is only partially implemented. `ManagerEventType` includes many events (`UNDERPERFORM`, `RETRY`, `REALLOCATE`, `EXCLUDE`, `ABORT`, `ROUND_START`, `MODEL_RESPONSE`), but the code emits only a small subset and never emits recovery actions despite claiming dynamic PM monitoring for recovery decisions. This matters because interface consumers cannot rely on the declared event protocol.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit all declared events at the relevant points: round start, model response receipt, underperformance detection, and every recovery action. Alternatively remove unused event types and narrow the contract.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F013  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: `update_fingerprints()` uses duplicate detection based solely on prior `finding_id` equality. Since finding IDs are typically round-unique, repeated findings with new IDs will not count as duplicates, so `D_decay` is systematically underestimated. This undermines the intended semantics of detection decay and makes adaptive updates misleading.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use equivalence-class novelty from `ConvergenceDetector` or a similarity function over finding content/class rather than raw ID equality.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F014  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `update_fingerprints()` only updates active models. Excluded/inactive models retain stale fingerprints indefinitely. If they are later reintroduced externally, their live state is inconsistent with observed history. This is a lifecycle gap in the adaptive model state.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either explicitly make exclusion permanent and document it, or continue updating/store terminal metrics for inactive models and define a reactivation path.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F015  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._solve_greedy()` intentionally force-assigns tasks even when doing so violates F1 token feasibility. Since F1 is documented as a HARD feasibility constraint, knowingly returning infeasible allocations violates the stated contract. Warning afterward does not restore correctness.  
PROPOSED_FIX: If no feasible assignment exists, return an explicit infeasibility result or raise an exception rather than manufacturing an infeasible allocation. If coverage is preferred over F1, reclassify/document the constraint accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F016  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._redundancy_target()` uses total model count `K = len(self.models)` rather than admissible/active worker count for the task. For high-criticality tasks, it may demand redundancy equal to all models even when PM is inadmissible, making the target unattainable by construction. The greedy solver silently underachieves the target.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base redundancy targets on admissible model count for the task, or cap the target by `sum(admissibility[j])`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F017  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `_admissibility_mask()` computes `k_total` from the number of entries in `role_map`, not from the actual model list passed to the load balancer. In a reduced active-model scenario, if `role_map` still contains inactive models, K=1 behavior can be misdetected. This matters because PM admissibility for single-model fallback can be wrong.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute total available models from `self.models` or the intersection of `self.models` and `role_map`, not all role-map entries.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F018  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.get_ordering()` returns the initial cached `capability_scores` and never reflects live fingerprint updates, failure-history penalties, or reassignments. Yet it presents itself as the role ordering relation. Consumers can receive stale, misleading rankings.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Recompute scores on demand from current active/live model state or rename this method to indicate it returns initial assignment ordering only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F019  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` computes `mu` using a direct check against the private dict `_cumulative_yields`, but `add_round_from_findings()` always inserts the round, making the condition redundant. More importantly, it reaches into private detector internals (`_novel_classes`, `_cumulative_yields`) instead of using public API. This is a maintenance/correctness smell that couples components tightly and makes invariants fragile.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Expose public methods for novel findings and round registration outcome, and remove direct private-member access from `DynamicManager`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F020  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: The `blind_first` config is marked HARD and documented as “always start with blind round,” but it is never consulted. The FSM always starts at `BLIND` regardless of config, making the parameter dead and misleading.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `blind_first` from config or enforce/validate it explicitly. If configurability is intended, use it in FSM initialization.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F021  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` takes `round_idx` but never uses it. This suggests an incomplete or misleading interface relative to documented “for failure history” behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove the unused parameter or use it to window failure history by round as intended.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F022  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56  
DESCRIPTION: `Allocation.model_load_fraction()` computes `m_idx` but never uses it. This is minor but indicates inattentive implementation around a core helper.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove the unused local variable.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F023  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54  
DESCRIPTION: Several imports are unused: `Literal`, `Protocol`, `Union` appear unused. This is minor but contributes to interface noise and hints at unfinished abstractions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove unused imports or complete the intended abstractions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F024  
SEVERITY: 0.65  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.validate_no_findings()` docstring says “not converged unless null_expected,” but the implementation only checks `kappa_set(2) == 1.0` and does not validate the non-convergence condition. The validator therefore does not test what its description claims.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update the validator to assert `not cd.converged(2)` under default config, or rewrite the docstring to match the actual test.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F025  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.53  
DESCRIPTION: `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop()` docstring says the ascending abstraction guard is conjunctive and part of the stop decision, but the implementation does not use `_abstraction_dropping()` at all. This is a direct spec/implementation mismatch.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either incorporate `_abstraction_dropping()` into `stop()` according to the intended conjunctive logic, or remove the claim from the docs and dead helper.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F026  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.59  
DESCRIPTION: The dispatch feasibility extension is not integrated into allocation or dispatch planning. `check_dispatch_feasibility()` exists as a standalone helper, but `get_allocation()` and `LoadBalancer.solve()` ignore `L_std` and feasibility probability. This leaves the extension operationally optional rather than part of the management layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Incorporate feasibility probability into admissibility or objective scoring during allocation, at least for uncertain-capacity models.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F027  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` uses single-linkage clustering. Similarity non-transitivity means two findings can be grouped into one class even if they are mutually below threshold via a bridging finding. For equivalence-class semantics this is questionable and can overmerge distinct findings, affecting convergence metrics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: If true equivalence is required, use complete-linkage or centroid-based clustering, or explicitly document that the relation is the transitive closure of threshold similarity.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F028  
SEVERITY: 0.62  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.estimate_gamma()` returns `inf` when cumulative findings are unchanged, which may be mathematically defensible for one parameterization but is not documented as a possible public return value beyond the broad description. This can surprise consumers expecting finite diagnostics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document `inf`/`0.0` edge semantics explicitly or return `None` for degenerate cases.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F029  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` does not emit an `UNDERPERFORM` event even though the event type exists and underperformance is a first-class failure type. This makes monitoring incomplete and inconsistent with the typed event interface.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` when underperformance is detected.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F030  
SEVERITY: 0.60  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` does not emit events for recovery actions (`RETRY`, `EXCLUDE`, `ABORT`, etc.) despite defining those event types and advertising real-time manager monitoring of recovery policy.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit a recovery event after deciding the action, including failure type and escalation metadata.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F031  
SEVERITY: 0.59  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: The smoke test prints “Phase 6 implementation complete” regardless of whether the integration meaningfully exercised all six areas. It does not process a round, so most orchestration paths remain untested. This overstates coverage.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace with a stronger integration test that exercises allocation, round processing, failure handling, convergence, stopping, and state transitions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F032  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundResult` has an `allocation` field, but `DynamicManager.process_round()` always sets it to `None` with a comment saying caller retains allocation reference. This weakens the cross-area contract promised by the dataclass and leaves round records incomplete.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Accept allocation as an argument to `process_round()` and store it in `RoundResult`, or remove the field from the result type.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F033  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.50  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.should_abort()` says “If only PM survives, framework degrades to single-model mode,” but the actual predicate is only `len(active_models) < k_min` with default `k_min=1`, so PM-only mode does not cause abort. The behavior is fine, but the logic about degradation is only in comments; there is no explicit mode handling.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either document that PM-only continuation follows implicitly from `k_min=1`, or add explicit single-model-mode signaling.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F034  
SEVERITY: 0.56  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: `ManagerEvent.model_id` is typed as `str`, but system-level events use `"system"` as a sentinel pseudo-model ID. This overloads model identity and event source identity, which can confuse consumers filtering by model.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a separate `source` field or allow `Optional[str]` for `model_id` on system events.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F035  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 3  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46  
DESCRIPTION: `_check_feasibility()` computes role violations as `matrix & ~admissibility` on integer arrays. It works for 0/1 matrices under current assumptions, but relies on bitwise complement semantics rather than clearer boolean logic. This is fragile if dtype or value conventions change.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use boolean arrays explicitly, e.g. `(matrix.astype(bool) & ~admissibility.astype(bool))`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F036  
SEVERITY: 0.54  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.45  
DESCRIPTION: `default_vulnerability` exists in config but is never used by `CorrelatedFailureModel`, whose default remains hardcoded to 0.0. This is a dead configuration parameter and a contract mismatch.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass config into `CorrelatedFailureModel` or use `default_vulnerability` in `get_vulnerability()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F037  
SEVERITY: 0.53  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43  
DESCRIPTION: `theta_col` exists in config with comment “only used if threshold-based COL selection is enabled,” but there is no threshold-based COL selection path. Another dead parameter weakens trust in the implementation/spec alignment.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Implement the threshold-based path or remove the parameter.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F038  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.42  
DESCRIPTION: `delta_deg` is configured as “degradation severity scaling” but is unused. This suggests incomplete failure-handling implementation around degrade semantics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Apply `delta_deg` in degradation logic or remove it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F039  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.42  
DESCRIPTION: `default_vulnerability`, `theta_col`, and `delta_deg` are not the only dead knobs; several config parameters are declared globally without full area ownership, increasing the risk of stale API surface.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Audit config for live references, remove unused fields, and add tests asserting every config field affects behavior or is intentionally reserved.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F040  
SEVERITY: 0.51  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundProgressionFSM.valid_events()` exposes `CONVERGED` and `DIMINISHED` in `SYNTH`, while the module examples and narrative imply iterative rounds begin after `SYNTH -> ROUND_1`. This may be intended, but it is underexplained and can terminate before any iterative round.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document that convergence/diminishing may terminate in SYNTH, or restrict those events to `ROUND_k` states if that is the intended protocol.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
